items.title: Can a crowd be better than the people in it? | Gustave Le Bon
items.description:
Think of the last time you were part of a crowd: a stadium, a protest, a packed train platform, a group chat that turned on someone.

Lessons and original commentary inspired by The Crowd by Gustave Le Bon. Modern exercises are our interpretations, not author quotations. Footage is illustrative, not historical or location evidence.

Chapters:

1:12 Why crowds get a bad name
2:18 The other side of the ledger
3:24 When self-interest switches off
4:29 Scoundrels with principles
5:33 What this does and does not prove
6:41 Reasoning is not always the hero

items.title: Do you hold contradictory beliefs at once? | Gustave Le Bon
items.description:
Do you hold contradictory beliefs at the same time without noticing?

MindLore explains psychology from the original texts. Original commentary inspired by The Crowd by Gustave Le Bon. Modern examples are our interpretations, not author quotations.

Chapters:
0:00 The Mental Glitch
1:10 The Common Belief
2:28 The Old Observation
3:50 Now vs Then
5:09 The Evidence
6:24 The Viewer's Doubt
7:38 The Takeaway

Part of the series "What Your Mind Actually Does", episode 8. New videos regularly.

Sources: The Crowd by Gustave Le Bon (original text, https://www.gutenberg.org/ebooks/445)

Evidence mentioned in this video:
- Kurt Lewin (1940s, Yale University): Group norms override individual logic, leading to actions against self-interest.
- Gustave Le Bon (1895, France): Fundamental ideas in crowds change slowly and persist for generations.

items.title: Why do you suddenly overthink a minor mistake? | Freud
items.description:
Why do you suddenly overthink a minor mistake when you are tired?

MindLore explains psychology from the original texts. Original commentary inspired by A General Introduction to Psychoanalysis by Sigmund Freud. Modern examples are our interpretations, not author quotations.

Chapters:
0:00 The Late Night Overthinking Trap
1:17 The Illusion of Rational Criticism
2:31 Freud's View on Intellectual Resistance
3:42 Modern Pressure vs Past Discovery
4:57 What Modern Neuroscience Confirms
6:13 Is Overthinking Always a Defense?
7:25 Breaking the Late Night Cycle

Part of the series "What Your Mind Actually Does", episode 10. New videos regularly.

Sources: A General Introduction to Psychoanalysis by Sigmund Freud (original text, https://www.gutenberg.org/ebooks/38219)

Evidence mentioned in this video:
- Matthew Walker and his research team (2007, University of California, Berkeley): Modern fMRI neuroimaging shows that sleep deprivation impairs prefrontal cortex control over the amygdala, leading to exaggerated emotional reactions to stress.
- Roy Baumeister (1998, Case Western Reserve University): Empirical studies on cognitive fatigue demonstrate that ego depletion decreases working memory capacity and accentuates automatic defensive biases.
